sources.entry: DavMail ⚠ - POP/IMAP/SMTP/Caldav/Carddav/LDAP exchange gateway allowing users to use any mail/calendar client with an Exchange server, even from the internet or behind a firewall through Outlook Web Access. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: DavMail is a gateway that lets standard mail, calendar and contact clients talk to Exchange and Office 365 servers through POP, IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV and LDAP.
summary.what_it_does: DavMail translates between common open protocols and Microsoft Exchange/Office 365, so any mail client that speaks POP, IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV or LDAP can access an Exchange account. The README describes it as a gateway for any mail client with Exchange and Office 365. It is distributed as packages for macOS, Linux and Windows. The README links to release downloads on SourceForge, RPM packages from the OpenSuse build service, COPR for Fedora, Flatpak, and Docker images on GitHub Container Registry. Trunk builds for Windows, Debian and macOS are published on Appveyor. This GitHub repository is a mirror synchronized with the project's Subversion repository. The README points to separate pages for setup and release notes, which are not included in it.
use_cases: Use Thunderbird or another IMAP client with an Exchange mailbox
Sync Exchange calendars to a CalDAV client
Sync Exchange contacts to a CardDAV client
Access Office 365 mail from a non-Outlook mail client
Reach an Exchange server from outside the corporate network
Run a local Exchange gateway in Docker
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the SourceForge project page, or install a package for your platform (RPM, COPR, Flatpak, Docker image, or Appveyor trunk build)
Follow the Getting Started guide referenced in the README
Configure your mail or calendar client to connect to the local DavMail server ports
notable: Supports both on-premises Exchange and Office 365
Covers mail, calendar, contacts and LDAP through one gateway
Packaged for Windows, macOS, Linux, Docker and Flatpak
Includes an embedded Java runtime in the Windows packages
Mirrors the SourceForge Subversion repository on GitHub
caveats: The README says the main project site is on SourceForge, and this GitHub repository is only a synchronized mirror
macOS setup notes say Azul JDK is preferred, and the Debian package depends on OpenJDK
Detailed setup and release information is in separate documents not included in the README
